one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Aastha Spintex Limited is a Gujarat-based B2B manufacturer of carded, combed and compact combed 100% cotton yarns and cotton bales, operating an integrated spinning-and-ginning facility at Halvad, Morbi.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Manufactures and trades carded, combed and compact combed cotton yarns (counts Ne 26 to Ne 40) and cotton bales at a semi-automated integrated spinning-and-ginning facility in Halvad, Morbi, Gujarat. Cotton bales are used both for captive yarn production and for sale to other spinning units; yarns serve knitting/weaving end-uses (denim, terry towels, shirting, sheeting, sweaters, socks, home and industrial textiles). Operates exclusively B2B, selling directly within Gujarat and, for out-of-state/export markets, through a reseller arrangement with 7 Seas Impex.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:
- Falcon Yarns Private Limited — Target company (acquisition funded by the Issue): Share purchase agreement dated Sept 22, 2025 at Rs 33.33/share; total consideration Rs 13,151 lakhs; promoters also on Falcon's board
- Devkinandan Paper Mills Private Limited — Group company: Promoter-group company
- Gyanmata Trading Private Limited — Group company: Promoter-group company
- 7 Seas Impex — Reseller: Facilitates out-of-Gujarat and export sales of cotton yarn

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Cotton Yarn:** 100% cotton yarn Ne 26-40, carded, combed, compact combed
- **Cotton Bales:** ginned cotton bales (captive + external sale)
- **By-products:** cotton seed (ginning by-product), cotton waste (comber, licker-in, hard waste from spinning)

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Textile manufacturers, yarn exporters, bulk purchasers, fabric processors (B2B)
- Denim, terry towels, shirting, sheeting, sweaters, socks, bottom wear, home textiles, industrial fabrics
- Cotton seed to oil-extraction/animal-feed industries; cotton waste to non-woven/open-end yarn makers
- Predominantly domestic (Gujarat direct; rest of India / exports via reseller 7 Seas Impex)

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Backward-integrated: an in-house ginning unit converts raw cotton into cotton bales (the principal raw material for spinning), providing raw-material security and by-product revenue (cotton seed, cotton waste). Ginning operates seasonally (~6-7 months, mid-Sept/Oct to March); shortfalls are met by sourcing bales from ginning mills/traders across Gujarat. Procurement is hedging-based (bales locked at order confirmation) with buffer stock built during the harvest season. Captive renewable power (1 MW rooftop solar, 4 MW ground solar, 2.7 MW wind) reduces power cost.

customers.title: Oem (RHP)
customers.body: 7 Seas Impex (reseller for out-of-Gujarat and export sales)

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Cotton bale (raw material) price exposure managed via order-linked hedging procurement and seasonal buffer stock
- Seasonal ginning unit (~6-7 months, mid-Sept/Oct to March) driving inventory build-up
- Customer concentration (top-10 customers 59.94% in FY2025) and supplier concentration (top-10 73.05% in FY2025)
- Captive renewable power reducing electricity cost
- Product mix between cotton yarn, cotton bales and by-products

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Acquire Falcon Yarns Private Limited to expand spinning capacity and scale
- Continue captive-renewable-power expansion to lower power costs
- Deepen B2B customer relationships and repeat-customer base
- Leverage reseller model (7 Seas Impex) for out-of-state and export reach

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The principal growth step is the acquisition of Falcon Yarns Private Limited (a spinning company) funded from the Issue proceeds (Rs 11,151 lakhs part payment plus Rs 1,000 lakhs inter-corporate deposit for Falcon's working capital), which adds spinning capacity and scale to the existing 25,920-spindle / 7,700 MT yarn and 12,000 MT cotton-bale integrated facility at Halvad. The company has also built captive renewable power (solar + wind) to reduce operating costs.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Integrated spinning-and-ginning operations providing raw-material (cotton bale) security and by-product revenue
- Highest ROCE and RONW amongst selected peers in Fiscal 2025 (per DRHP)
- Captive renewable power (1 MW rooftop + 4 MW ground solar + 2.7 MW wind) reducing power cost
- Location advantage in Halvad, Morbi near high-quality Gujarat cotton-growing area
- Hedging-based procurement approach locking cotton bale prices at order confirmation
- Long-standing customer/supplier relationships (>250 customers over 3 years; 14 associated >5 years)

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Acquisition of Falcon Yarns at a premium to its recent buyback price — Acquisition at Rs 33.33/share vs Falcon's Sept-2024 buyback at Rs 14.46/share; ~Rs 11,151 lakhs of Issue proceeds deployed; integration and valuation risk
- Customer concentration — Top-10 customers were 59.94% (FY25), 84.71% (FY24), 80.88% (FY23) of product sales
- Supplier concentration — Top-10 suppliers were 73.05% (FY25), 79.62% (FY24), 44.30% (FY23) of purchases
- Cotton price volatility — Cotton bale is the principal raw material; price swings and seasonal availability affect margins despite hedging
- Reseller dependence for out-of-state/export sales — Reliance on 7 Seas Impex for markets outside Gujarat
- Single-facility / geographic concentration — All operations at one facility in Halvad, Morbi, Gujarat
- Working-capital intensity / seasonal buffer stock — Buffer cotton-bale stock during harvest season raises inventory and working-capital needs

commitments.title: Promises (RHP)
commitments.body:
- **Acquire Falcon Yarns Private Limited using Rs 11,151 lakhs of Issue proceeds toward part payment of the Rs 13,151 lakhs consideration**
- **Provide Rs 1,000 lakhs inter-corporate deposit to fund Falcon Yarns' working capital**
- **Operate 25,920-spindle / 7,700 MT p.a. cotton yarn and 12,000 MT p.a. cotton bale integrated capacity**
- **Continue captive renewable power (1 MW rooftop solar, 4 MW ground solar, 2.7 MW wind) to reduce power cost**

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Acquire Falcon Yarns Private Limited to expand spinning capacity and scale
- Continue captive-renewable-power expansion to lower power costs
- Deepen B2B customer relationships and repeat-customer base
- Leverage reseller model (7 Seas Impex) for out-of-state and export reach
